downstream_writing.pr_description:
Reject a Pair-stride body with an odd entry count before choosing a split. Previously, five entries could produce a 2|3 split whose cursor was pair-aligned even though the right side contained a partial pair. `split_point` now returns `DecodeError::Corrupt` for that body.

The guard must precede both division by the stride and the early return for at most one unit: integer division would otherwise discard the remainder. Review `crates/data-structure/ziplist/src/chain.rs:351`. Split targets count encoded entry bytes, excluding the 12-byte header. Callers budgeting full chunks must add one header per side; callers passing `used_len()` to `should_merge` must first subtract the header. The merge predicate is unchanged; its renamed parameters make this convention explicit (`chain.rs:388`).

downstream_writing.pr_description:
`split_point` now rejects bodies whose entry count is not a whole number of logical units. With pair stride, a five-entry body previously admitted a 2|3 split despite a pair-aligned cursor; it now returns `DecodeError::Corrupt`.

Split and merge sizes count encoded entries, excluding the block header. The `should_merge` parameter names now express that convention; its saturating half-target calculation is unchanged. Callers using `used_len()` must subtract `HEADER_SIZE` from each block size.

Review the alignment guard before unit-count division and the early `None` return at `crates/data-structure/ziplist/src/chain.rs:351`. The strengthened conservation test at `crates/data-structure/ziplist/src/chain.rs:1368` walks both sides independently: deriving the right count by subtraction would make the entry-total assertion tautological. Both walks advance forward. The test checks whole units on each side and sums walked entry lengths for byte conservation.
